the synthesis of a novel donor-acceptor system (7) and the investigation of its ground-state and excited-state properties.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have synthesized a new fullerene-based dyads, which exhibits strong electronic coupling between donor and acceptor moieties in the ground state as well as in the electronically excited state.
the electronic coupling between the donor and acceptor groups in a dyad is strongly influenced by their spatial arrangement.

the present dyad represents the first example where two electroactive units are directly bonded via a single sigma-bonds and that the strong electronic coupling between both units is clearly evidenced by electrochemical and photophysical measurements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ground and the excited state properties of 7 are dominated by the electronic coupling between the two electroactive groups.
the electronic coupling in the ground state is much stronger than in the excited state, which is in stark contrast to the situation in the corresponding donor-acceptor systems based on C60.
